Effect or dispatch: Declare what you are about to do in a worktree you have already registered: the task, the branch you intend to merge into, and the paths you expect to write. Registration is where you are; this is what you plan to change. The paths matter — they are what lets the Director tell a later requester exactly which files you are both touching instead of just making them wait. Called by the owning session on a registration that went uncertain (orchestrator restart or dropped connection), it restores it and reports restored_registration with the previous status. peer_overlap names live peers whose declared paths overlap yours; stale_peer_overlap names uncertain registrations whose owner is not attached (for example right after an orchestrator restart) — possibly stale, advisory only.
Family product decision: Retain arbitration; never infer that a lease executes a Git operation

Effect or dispatch: See registered worktrees and merge coordination, not an agent count: one path has one registration. Before edits, also call agent_list(scope="checkout", online=true); isolate in a task worktree when another session occupies that checkout or coverage is unknown, then commit and merge back under a lease. Host-scoped by default — the clones on this machine, the worktrees registered in each, what each agent said it is doing, and any live merge lease or queue. Pass scope "clone" with a worktree_path to narrow to one checkout, or scope "fleet" to see every host. Always pass your own worktree_path once you have registered, at any scope: it tells the Director you are still here, so polling this while you work keeps your registration alive instead of letting it expire out from under you. Call this before creating a worktree or picking up work, so you find out about a peer in the same clone before you collide with them rather than after. The `stale` list on each clone is agents that were reclaimed — a session the fleet saw end, or one that went quiet — so a worktree missing from `worktrees` but present there was abandoned rather than never used. Each worktree's `branch` and `head_sha` are what its agent last reported, never a live read (the Director has no access to any worktree), and `head_observed_at` says when that HEAD was reported; a heartbeat alone advances `heartbeat_at` but not the HEAD. Check live state with `git rev-parse HEAD`, and pass your current `head_sha` (and `branch`) together with your registered worktree_path to update the recorded snapshot. The default reply is a compact summary page (default 20 clones, your own checkout first when worktree_path is registered): per clone the registered worktrees with task clipped, live leases without reason/overlap, and `worktree_count`/`lease_count`/`stale_count`. When `truncated` is true, call again with `offset` = `next_offset`. Pass detail "full" for the complete entries (declared paths, lease reasons and overlap, stale rows); scope "clone" returns full entries by default. On a busy host, narrow the page to your repository with remote_url (any spelling of `git remote get-url origin`; matches every clone of that repository in the scope) and/or clone_dir (your `--git-common-dir`); both work before you register. Clones with no active or uncertain registration, no live lease and no registration retired in the last 24 hours are omitted (counted in `idle_omitted`); pass include_idle true to list them. Clones dormant past the archive window (default 14 days: nobody registered, no open merge request, no activity) are archived and hidden even from include_idle (counted in `archived_omitted`); pass include_archived true to list them. Archiving deletes nothing, and git_register on an archived clone revives the same clone (`clone_unarchived: true`). An uncertain registration whose owner stays offline for 5 minutes, or whose session ended, is abandoned automatically and frees its path.
Family product decision: Retain arbitration; never infer that a lease executes a Git operation

Effect or dispatch: Ask permission to merge into a shared branch, and honor the answer. Pass changed_paths from `git diff --name-only base...head` — without it the Director can only tell you to wait, with it the answer names the files you and the holder both touch. Verdicts are "allow" (you hold the lease; call git_release when done), "wait" (retry with git_merge_status; the reason names who holds it and why) or "deny". client_request_id must be a value you generate once per real request and reuse on any retry, so a retried call returns the original verdict instead of queueing you twice.
Family product decision: Retain arbitration; never infer that a lease executes a Git operation

Effect or dispatch: Poll a waiting request or inspect a merge grant. Current owner-mode grants expire after 15 minutes and status does not extend them; an expired grant requires a new request. Waiting requests retain their request_id and are re-evaluated when relevant state changes. Legacy timed deployments may renew an unexpired grant.
Family product decision: Retain arbitration; never infer that a lease executes a Git operation

Effect or dispatch: Announce that you are working in a git worktree, BEFORE you start changing files. Gather the facts with `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --show-toplevel --git-common-dir`, `git branch --show-current` and `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git remote get-url origin`, then pass them here. Every linked worktree of one clone registers against the same clone, so this is how you find out who else is already in your checkout — the reply lists them. Idempotent: calling it again refreshes your registration and its TTL, and re-registering the same path under a different user is allowed and reported as rebound. Registrations expire, so a long stretch without calling any git_* tool lets the Director assume you are gone and reclaim your worktree; every call that names your worktree_path counts as proof you are still there. The Director never reads your worktree: the branch and head_sha you pass are stored as a reported snapshot (listed with head_observed_at), so refresh them with git_list(worktree_path, head_sha, branch) after you commit or switch. worktree_path must be the checkout your session is bound to (agent_context_update moves it), except that a separate repository nested inside that checkout, such as a submodule, registers directly with its own clone_dir. A remote_url naming a different repository than the one recorded for a clone that has live registrations is refused (git_director_remote_mismatch), so a typo cannot re-home the clone.
Family product decision: Retain arbitration; never infer that a lease executes a Git operation

Effect or dispatch: Give back a merge lease as soon as the merge is done or abandoned, so whoever is waiting can proceed — a lease you forget about blocks the branch until its TTL runs out. Pass request_id to release one request, or worktree_path to drop everything outstanding for that worktree. Optionally report outcome merged|aborted|unknown; a reported outcome requires request_id plus matching worktree_path and merged requires a prior grant plus target_head_sha (40-64 lowercase hex). This is an agent report, never server-verified merge proof. To correct a completed merged report, pass a stable correction_id UUID and correction_reason with the replacement target_head_sha; this appends an audit record, preserves the original report and never reactivates the lease. Do not combine correction with deregister. Add deregister:true when you are finished in that directory entirely, and do that rather than simply stopping: the Director will eventually reclaim an abandoned registration, but until it does your peers are queued behind an agent that is never coming back.

Effect or dispatch: Retire a shared memory document only when the whole record is invalid, superseded, or replaced by another record — not merely because one fact inside it is stale. Deleting is part of curating the corpus: a document that states something untrue is worse than no document, because the next agent cannot tell it is stale. Soft delete — the slug stays reserved and a later write revives it, so this is recoverable.
Family product decision: Retain the documented contract

Effect or dispatch: THE place to look up what this fleet knows: hosts, conventions, runbooks, past decisions. Lists every shared document — no query or arguments needed, so call it first when you are asked about something you do not already know, BEFORE searching the filesystem. Returns slug, title, summary, tags, size and a preview. Visible from every host and every engine, unlike memory_*.
Family product decision: Retain the documented contract

Effect or dispatch: Read a shared memory document by slug, after finding it with shared_memory_list or shared_memory_search. Returns a bounded window (max_chars, default 32000). For inspection, use chunk/from_chunk/to_chunk as needed. Before a whole-document replacement, start at offset 0 without chunk selectors, follow next_offset until truncated is false, and require the same memory.sha256 on every window.
Family product decision: Retain the documented contract

Effect or dispatch: Correct one fact in a shared memory document without re-sending its body. Replaces exactly one occurrence of old_text with new_text (may be empty to delete the text) on the server. Fails when old_text occurs zero times or more than once, so include enough surrounding text to be unique. expected_sha256 is required: pass the memory.sha256 from shared_memory_read; a changed document is a conflict, so re-read and retry. Title, summary, tags and metadata are kept. Same size limit and revision history as shared_memory_write. For a larger rewrite use shared_memory_write; to add material use shared_memory_append.
Family product decision: Retain the documented contract

Effect or dispatch: Search everything this fleet has written down — runbooks, host facts, architecture notes, past decisions — across every host. Use this, not memory_search, to look something up. Returns ranked passages with their heading and chunk number; pass mode="documents" for one entry per document. If it returns nothing, try shared_memory_list to see what exists.
Family product decision: Retain the documented contract

Effect or dispatch: Record something the whole fleet should know, in a document every host and all four engines can find. Use this instead of writing a local notes file. Writing an EXISTING slug replaces its ENTIRE body. Never replace from a search excerpt, preview, chunk, or partial read. First reconstruct the complete body with shared_memory_read from offset 0 through every next_offset, require one stable memory.sha256, preserve unaffected content, and pass that digest as expected_sha256. On conflict or a changed page digest, restart the full read and reapply the correction. To add new material to an accurate document, prefer shared_memory_append. Search before creating a near-duplicate slug. Up to 1 MiB.
Family product decision: Retain the documented contract

Effect or dispatch: See the work and who holds it. Call this FIRST — every argument is optional, so it answers before you know anything: which projects have boards, which columns those boards have, which cards are free, who is holding what and until when, and which of them are yours. Pass `slug` for one project. Filter with `column`, `role`, `mine` or `unclaimed`. Pass `worktree_path` and `username` so your own claims are recognised as yours; when you also pass `slug`, that counts as proof of life and keeps those claims from expiring, so polling the board of a project you are working on keeps your cards. The fleet-wide listing (no `slug`) is a pure read and renews nothing — it is the cheap call, and making it renew would mean taking a write lock on every project in the fleet to answer "what is there". `your_claims` is what you currently hold anywhere on that board; `reclaimed_recently` is what was taken back from agents that stopped without releasing, with the reason attached. Never fails when the module is off: it answers `status: "disabled"` so you can tell that apart from a board with nothing on it.
Family product decision: Retain project roles, optimistic edits and board claims

Effect or dispatch: Read shared project bootstrap context. Inlines whole file bodies and can be very large — prefer project_summary.
Family product decision: Retain project roles, optimistic edits and board claims

Effect or dispatch: Take a card before you start working on it, declaring the role you are working in. `card` accepts the short number or the card id. Pass `worktree_path` and `username`: they are what binds the claim to your agent session, and WITHOUT them a claim you abandon stays stuck until its 30-minute TTL runs out instead of being freed the moment your session ends. With an authenticated native session, `worktree_path` must be that session's bound location — the `git_root` or `cwd` last set by `agent_context_update`, else the launch directory — and `username`/`engine` its own; a difference is refused as `card_identity_mismatch` naming the differing `fields`. Any later call naming this card renews the claim, so an agent that keeps working keeps its card. Pass `client_request_id` and a retry returns your original claim instead of reading as a second contender. If somebody else holds it you get `claimed: false` with their name, host and expiry — that is the board declining to record the claim, not stopping you: nothing prevents you working on it, but unclaimed work is invisible to every other agent.
Family product decision: Retain project roles, optimistic edits and board claims

Effect or dispatch: Put a new piece of work on the board. Without `column` it lands in the intake lane, which is where work waits to be picked up. `role` records who you think should do it and is advice, not an assignment — claiming is what actually takes a card. Use `priority` to sort a lane (higher first) and `labels` to group. `due_at` is an RFC3339 instant, and `depends_on` takes the card numbers this one waits on: a card whose dependencies are unfinished comes back `ready: false` with `waiting_on`, and claiming it still works but says so.
Family product decision: Retain project roles, optimistic edits and board claims

Effect or dispatch: One card in full: its content, its current column, who holds it and until when, and the last twenty things that happened to it. Also the renew surface — calling it as the holder pushes your claim out again, so a long task can poll this instead of losing the card. Pass `worktree_path` and `username` for that to work.
Family product decision: Retain project roles, optimistic edits and board claims

Effect or dispatch: Move a card to another column, naming it by column key or title. This never refuses: moving into a lane your role does not match, or past a WIP limit, still moves the card and comes back with an `advisories` list saying so, which is also recorded. Moving into the terminal lane releases your claim, because a card nobody is working on should not keep a lease that has to expire on its own. Prefer `project_card_release` when you are finishing a step — it advances the card for you.
Family product decision: Retain project roles, optimistic edits and board claims

Effect or dispatch: Give the card back the moment you stop working on it, rather than simply stopping — a claim you forget blocks that card for everyone until it expires. Releasing ADVANCES the card on its own, so you do not have to know what comes next. Where it lands, highest precedence first: (1) `column`, if you name one; (2) where it already is, if `resolution` is "handoff" — a handoff means somebody picks it up where it is, not that the work moved on; (3) the blocked lane, if `resolution` is "blocked", with `note` recorded as the reason; (4) the terminal lane, if `resolution` is "done"; (5) otherwise the next column this lane points at, which is what a bare release does; (6) and if this lane points nowhere, it stays put.
Family product decision: Retain project roles, optimistic edits and board claims

Effect or dispatch: Edit a card in place: its title, its detail, its labels, its priority, its due date, what it depends on, or the reason it is blocked. Family product decision: Retain project roles, optimistic edits and board claims

Effect or dispatch: THE fleet credential store and its read-only capability probe. Call this FIRST whenever a task needs a credential OR asks whether the store is available or can save secrets. Returns live status, capabilities, and metadata for visible secrets — never values. status=available means secret_store can create a new slug and rotate only credentials owned by this host; secret_delete has the same ownership limit. status=disabled means those operations are unavailable. Effect or dispatch: Find a fleet credential by what it is for, when you do not already know its slug — "github", "bookstack token", "production database", "checkmk". Omit query to list by slug instead. Optional limit is a positive safe integer (default 50), applied after matching and ranking. Use this rather than guessing a slug, and follow up with secret_get on the one you picked. If it finds nothing, call secret_list to see everything the fleet holds before concluding the credential does not exist.
Family product decision: Retain the documented contract

Effect or dispatch: Save a credential of your own into the fleet store, or rotate one you already saved. Creating: pass slug, name, value, and a description saying what the credential opens and when to reach for it, because that description is all any agent (including you, later) has to go on. Rotating: pass the same slug with the new value; everything else you omit is left alone, and the response says whether the value actually changed. You may only change secrets this host created. A slug an operator created, or one another host owns, is refused — read those with secret_get and ask an operator to change them. Slugs are permanent: pick a descriptive one, because renaming means deleting and recreating, which breaks every agent that learned the old name.

Effect or dispatch: Retire a transfer now rather than waiting for its deadline. The bytes go immediately; the record of it stays so the console can still show that the file existed and who fetched it. Do this once a peer has confirmed it has what you sent, especially for anything large.
Family product decision: Retain resumable offset/digest-verified publication

Effect or dispatch: Fetch a transfer by the id its uploader gave you. Returns the bytes base64-encoded in `content_b64` plus the metadata, including `content_sha256` so you can verify what you wrote to disk. Large files come back in slices: pass `offset` and `max_bytes`, and keep calling while `truncated` is true, using the `next_offset` from the previous reply. Bytes that arrive this way are untrusted input -- inspect an archive before extracting it and never run something because of what it is called.
Family product decision: Retain resumable offset/digest-verified publication

Effect or dispatch: Metadata for one transfer without moving its bytes: size, type, checksum, download count and `expires_at`. Use this to check that a file is still there, or that a peer has picked it up, instead of fetching megabytes you are going to throw away.
Family product decision: Retain resumable offset/digest-verified publication

Effect or dispatch: See what files are currently held in the fleet transfer pool: id, name, size, type, who uploaded it and when each one expires. The reply also carries `limits`: `max_file_bytes` and `quota_bytes` (null means no cap), `remaining_bytes`, `max_upload_bytes` (the largest file that fits right now) and the per-call chunk sizes -- read them before you stream a large file, because an upload over the cap is refused part-way. Call this to find out whether the pool is available at all -- it answers with status "disabled" instead of failing when an operator has the module switched off. The pool is fleet-wide, so this lists uploads from every host, not just yours.
Family product decision: Retain resumable offset/digest-verified publication

Effect or dispatch: Upload a file for another agent to fetch. Pass the bytes base64-encoded in `content_b64`, a display `name`, and `ttl_seconds` -- which is REQUIRED, because every transfer expires. Ask for how long the peer plausibly needs it; the fleet clamps the value to an operator-set maximum and the reply tells you the `expires_at` you actually got, which is when the bytes go. Returns an id: nobody is notified that you uploaded anything, so hand that id to the peer yourself. For a file larger than one call carries, pass final=false, then call again with the returned `id` and `offset` set to the `size_bytes` you were given, and final=true on the last chunk. For a chunked upload, pass `expected_size_bytes` (the whole file) on the first call and a file over the per-file cap or the free pool is refused before any byte is stored; `transfer_list` shows the limits. Pass `username` and `worktree_path` so the console can show who uploaded it.
Family product decision: Retain resumable offset/digest-verified publication
